# Dr. Gabriel Fahrenheit

## Description
Thin, elderly, wrapped in three scarves and an academic gown, with ink on his nose and
a speaking-trumpet under one arm. Blinks against the snow while explaining that it is
not, strictly, snowing. Has a cat called Mercury that he addresses as a colleague.

## Personality & motivation
Pedantic, brilliant, utterly committed to being right in the face of the weather. He
predicted clear skies and the passes open by noon; the instruments agree with him; the
sky does not; he sides with the instruments. He wants his forecast vindicated. He would
never falsify a reading. He will, if treated as a scholar, become a genuinely useful one.

## Knowledge & secrets
- Freely shares: the 07:00 forecast ("clear, bright, passes open by noon"); the castle's circuit, with times, from the telescope (over Widow's Ridge at 14:00, "disgracefully low"); the old Midwinter song, all nine verses, and his chart of the Crown with five stones named Toast, Dance, Song, Morning-After, Prudence, which he collects as folklore; the shadow-ometer: "every shadow in this town points at the Keep. I have measured it. The instrument reads KEEP. This is the control. Do not touch the control"
- Needs persuasion (DC 12) or any scholarly interest: the barometer is not moving; it has not moved since he woke; this is physically impossible and he is "looking into it"; the Almanac's page for Day 2 will not take ink
- Needs trust (DC 15, or shown the danger stone): he will identify the danger stone at sight as "Prudence, the fifth stone, which the song says sits in the Crown and tells the king when not to do a thing." He concludes, correctly and with great excitement, that someone has pried it out, and that the other four must have "gone where the song says they belong: a toast, a dance, a song, a sting"
